MINUTES
  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  WEDNESDAY, APRIL 8, 2026

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

CHAIR STEGURA called the meeting of the Environmental Advisory Committee Meeting of
the City of Rolling Hills Estates at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  ROLL CALL

Committee Members Present:  Stegura, Repp-Loadsman, Bain, Frias, McBurney,
  Mondkar, Rein

Committee Members Absent:  Uppal

City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Dev/Public Works Director
  Denise Jaramillo, Administrative Assistant

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING MINUTES,
  MAY 21, 2025.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
  MONDKAR TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  APPROVE THE CORRECTED ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE
  MEEETING MINUTES OF MAY 21, 2025.

There being no objection, CHAIR STEGURA so ordered.

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  CPA POWER READY PROGRAM: EQUIPMENT LOCATION ON CITY HALL
  PROPERTY

Director Naughton presented an overview of the City’s participation in the Clean Power
Alliance (CPA) Power Ready Program in 2025, which provides solar generation and battery
storage for critical facilities at no upfront cost to the city. City Hall qualifies as a critical facility
due to its role as an emergency operations center. The proposed system includes a
13‑kilowatt DC solar array on the south-facing roof of City Hall and a battery system capable
of supporting critical loads, including HVAC, servers, and kitchen equipment, for up to eight
hours during an outage. Annual electricity costs are guaranteed to be equal to or less than
current costs. The battery unit equipment area measures approximately 10 feet by 12 feet
and would be similar in appearance to existing electrical infrastructure on site. ARUP, CPA’s
technical consultant, identified several viable battery locations within landscaped areas near
City Hall and recommended locating the unit closest to the electrical switch for efficiency.

Staff recommends that the Environmental Advisory Committee discuss the potential battery
placement locations and provide a recommended location to the City Council.

CHAIR STEGURA asked whether the proposed equipment would be similar to the existing
electric vehicle charging equipment. Director Naughton confirmed it would be similar. The
Committee agreed to conduct a site walk to review potential locations.

The Committee discussed multiple potential locations for the battery system throughout the
City Hall property. CHAIR STEGURA and Committee Members raised concerns related to
visual impacts, proximity to City Hall, noise, landscaping, tree impacts, trenching

 requirements, safety, and vandalism. Locations near primary entrances and office areas
were generally viewed as less desirable.

COMMISSIONER REPP‑LOADSMAN supported locations that could be effectively
landscaped and would limit visual and operational impacts. COMMITTEE MEMBER
MONDKAR favored the red-marked location due to its proximity to existing infrastructure and
ability to be screened by landscaping. COMMISSIONER BAIN expressed concerns
regarding tree impacts and potential noise effects on wildlife. COMMITTEE MEMBER REIN
and FRIAS supported the Crenshaw Boulevard location, noting that it was farther from the
building and would minimize impacts to City Hall operations.

Director Naughton clarified that Clean Power Alliance would be responsible for all
installation, equipment, and maintenance costs, that the battery would provide approximately
eight hours of power to critical City Hall functions, and that the City’s existing generator could
provide additional backup power if needed.

After discussion, the Committee agreed to recommend the Crenshaw Boulevard location as
the first preference, with the location recommended by CPA and identified as Number Four
as the second preference. The Committee also agreed that staff should continue to
coordinate with the contractor and that a site walk should be conducted to further evaluate
the proposed locations.

  COMMISSIONER  REPP-LOADSMAN made  a  motion, seconded by
  COMMISSIONER BAIN TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL
  CALL VOTE:

  RECOMMEND THAT THE CITY COUNCIL SELECT LOCATION NO. 1 AS
  THE PREFERRED LOCATION, WITH LOCATION NO. 4 AS THE
  ALTERNATIVE, BOTH SUBJECT TO SCREENING, EVALUATION OF TREE
  CLEARANCE, INCLUSION OF TRENCHING, AND FULL PROJECT COSTS
  COVERED BY THE PROVIDER EXCEPT LANDSCAPING.

  Ayes:  Stegura, Repp-Loadsman, Bain, Frias, McBurney, Mondkar, Rein
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Uppal
  Abstain:  None

B.  CPA GREEN LEADER PROGRAM; SBCCOG GREEN BUSINESS PROGRAM

Director Naughton presented a staff report on the Clean Power Alliance Green Leader
Program and the South Bay City’s Council of Government Green Business Assist Program,
two free, voluntary programs that recognize environmental leadership among local
businesses. She noted that the programs provide promotional recognition, education, and
technical assistance, support participation in sustainability practices, fulfill General Plan IM
Energy 9.1.5, and offer recognition pathways for businesses both enrolled and not enrolled
in 100% clean energy.

Staff is seeking a recommendation from the Environmental Advisory Committee to move
forward with participation in these respective programs and partnering with the Chamber to
promote these programs through the City’s social media platforms, e-newsletters, and
business license communication.

CHAIR STEGURA explained that the sustainability element is part of the City’s 2040 General
Plan, funded through a state grant, and that the current item is consistent with that effort.
She asked about the marketing plan, noting staff’s intent to work with the Chamber, and
invited additional questions.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked about the division of responsibilities between
City staff and outside agencies. Director Naughton responded that Clean Power Alliance
(CPA) and the South Bay Cities Council of Governments (COG) administer the programs
and provide incentives, while City staff would focus on community outreach and information,
in partnership with the Chamber.

 COMMITTEE MEMBER MONDKAR highlighted the benefits of being a Certified Green
Business, including rebates, energy and water conservation upgrades, educational
resources, and advantages such as priority consideration for government contracts. In
response to Commissioner Bain’s question, she noted that customers, especially public
agencies, do seek out certified green businesses, adding that sustainability certification is
becoming increasingly important ahead of the LA28 Olympic Games.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER
  MONDKAR TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  RECOMMEND THAT THE CITY MOVE FORWARD WITH PARTICIPATION
  IN THE CLEAN POWER ALLIANCE AND SOUTH BAY CITIES COUNCIL OF
  GOVERNMENTS PROGRAMS AND PARTNER WITH THE CHAMBER OF
  COMMERCE FOR PROMOTION.

  Ayes:  Stegura, Repp-Loadsman, Bain, Frias, McBurney, Mondkar, Rein
  Noes:  None
  Absent:  Uppal
  Abstain:  None

C.  PROGRAM DEVELOPMENT: ZERO WASTE EVENTS

Director Naughton stated that the item was prompted by a resident concern regarding
streamer and Mylar balloon debris observed following a city parade. Staff proposed exploring
a waste-reduction program for City-sponsored and permitted events to support the City’s
Sustainability Element (IMWSD-9.3.4), align with Assembly Bill 2176, and reduce landfill
waste through reduce, reuse, and recycle practices. Director Naughton noted that the item
was presented to seek initial direction from the Environmental Advisory Committee, as no
formal program framework has been developed.

CHAIR STEGURA stated that the proposed waste-reduction approach would apply to
City-sponsored events such as the Street Fair, the Mayor’s Ride, and parades.

COMMITTEE MEMBER REIN questioned whether materials used at permitted events are
truly recyclable and cautioned that the term “zero waste” may be misleading. Chair Stegura
described a framework for larger events with separate waste streams and noted that
compliance would be required through the permitting process.

COMMISSIONER REP-LOADSMAN supported reducing waste at the source by restricting
allowable materials, including requiring compostable food service items and prohibiting Mylar
balloons. COMMISSIONER BAIN recommended routing the matter to the Parks and
Activities Commission, and the Committee agreed.

Members discussed Waste Management’s role, potential impacts on City maintenance staff,
the need to establish an event size threshold, and any necessary training for staff and event
organizers to implement waste-reduction requirements.

CHAIR STEGURA clarified that the proposal would move from the Committee to the Parks
and Activities Commission for review, with an education period prior to any future
enforcement. Director Naughton explained that the program would apply not only to city park
activities, but also to special event permits on private property, city-sponsored events, and
events in the public right-of-way. She recommended that staff conduct further research and
return to the EAC with a proposed framework prior to bringing the item to the Parks and
Activities Commission.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER MCBURNEY made a motion, seconded by
  COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE
  FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE: DIRECT STAFF TO CONDUCT
  ADDITIONAL RESEARCH ON THE PROPOSED PROGRAM AND RETURN
  TO THE ENVIRONMENTAL COMMITTEE WITH A PROPOSED
  FRAMEWORK PRIOR TO BRINGING THE ITEM TO THE PARKS AND
  ACTIVITIES COMMISSION.

  Noes:  None

6.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

Director Naughton provided an update on the upcoming Earth Day Event. She noted that the
event will be held on Thursday, April 23, from 3:30 p.m. to 6:00 p.m., and that this is the first
year the event will be hosted at City Hall, rather than at the Promenade as in prior years.

Director Naughton announced a Fire Defensible Planting and Home Protection Workshop to
be held on Thursday, May 14, from 6:00 to 8:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers, covering
home protection, defensible space, and fire‑resistant landscaping.

11.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

CHAIR STEGURA revisited a prior suggestion related to SB 1383 compliance and the
possibility of offering free compost to residents, similar to the City’s sandbag program. She
suggested exploring a partnership with Waste Management to provide compost at the Ernie
Howlett utility yard for resident pickup to support home gardening.

COMMITTEE MEMBER MONDKAR inquired about the City’s participation in the Blue Zones
program, noting its alignment with sustainability goals such as healthy food consumption,
waste reduction, local food production, and reduced transportation impacts. She observed
that several nearby beach cities participate and that many local restaurants are Blue Zone
certified.

COMMITTEE MEMBER FRIAS proposed composting as a future agenda item and
suggested a community composting workshop, potentially in conjunction with Earth Day or
a future event. Commissioner Repp-Loadsman recommended partnering with the South
Coast Botanic Garden for a composting demonstration.

12.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR STEGURA adjourned the meeting at 8:25 p.m.

Respectfully submitted by,  Approved,

Denise Jaramillo, Administrative Assistant  Debby Stegura, Chair
